beats: GRANDMA'S LAND. TWELVE OWNERS.
Land inherited with no will becomes heirs' property: every heir owns a share of the whole.
No one can sell, lease or mortgage it without ALL the heirs agreeing. Each generation adds more owners.
One mechanism. Know it early.
items.yt_title: What Is Heirs Property? Why Family Land Gets Stuck
items.tt_title: Why family land gets stuck with no will. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
Land passed down without a will becomes heirs' property: the descendants each own a share of the whole parcel, and USDA notes they can use the land but hold no clear, marketable title. Selling, leasing or mortgaging it takes every heir's agreement, and each generation adds more owners. If your family holds land this way, name it early and get help clearing title.

General info, not legal advice. Laws vary by state. Source: USDA, farmers.gov. AI-made visuals.
#wellkept #heirsproperty #familyland #generationalwealth

beats: SKIP PROBATE? THERE'S A DEED FOR THAT.
Texas lets a homeowner record a Transfer on Death Deed: the home passes to a named person without probate.
It only works if recorded in the county BEFORE death, and you can revoke it while you live.
Texas Estates Code, chapter 114.
items.source_chip: Source: TexasLawHelp / Tex. Estates Code ch. 114
items.yt_title: Transfer on Death Deed in Texas, Explained in 10 Seconds
items.tt_title: The Texas deed that skips probate. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
Since 2015, Texas Estates Code chapter 114 lets a homeowner record a Transfer on Death Deed naming who gets the home when they die, without probate. Two catches: it must be recorded in the county where the property sits before the owner dies, and the owner can revoke or change it any time while competent. If it conflicts with the will, the recorded deed controls the property.

General info, not legal advice. Laws vary by state. Source: TexasLawHelp.org; Texas Estates Code ch. 114. AI-made visuals.
#wellkept #transferondeathdeed #texas #estateplanning

beats: A TWO-YEAR CLOCK NOBODY MENTIONS.

If there's no eligible spouse, an eligible child can receive it.
Apply within 2 years of the death.
items.yt_title: Social Security's One-Time Death Payment: Who Can Claim It
items.tt_title: The $255 payment and its 2-year clock. Not legal advice.
items.caption:

General info, not legal advice. Source: SSA.gov. AI-made visuals.

beats: TWO BREAKS. ONE FORM. ONE DEADLINE.
Florida homesteads get a $25,000 exemption on all property taxes, plus up to about $25,000 more above $50,000 of value (non-school taxes).
You must be the permanent resident on January 1 and file with the property appraiser by March 1.
Mark the date.
items.yt_title: Florida Homestead Exemption: The March 1 Rule
items.tt_title: Florida's two homestead breaks and the deadline. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
Florida's homestead exemption comes in two parts: $25,000 off assessed value for all levies, and a second exemption of up to about $25,000 (inflation-adjusted, non-school taxes) on value above $50,000. The mechanism people miss: you need permanent Florida residency on January 1 and an application to the county property appraiser by March 1.

General info, not legal advice. Laws vary by state. Source: Florida Department of Revenue, PT-113. AI-made visuals.
#wellkept #homestead #florida #propertytax

beats: THE BILL THAT ARRIVES AFTER A FUNERAL.
Federal law makes states recover long-term-care Medicaid costs, for enrollees 55 and older, from the estate after death.
States must waive recovery that would cause hardship; rules and reach vary by state.
Ask about it BEFORE care starts.
items.yt_title: Medicaid Estate Recovery: What Families Learn Too Late
items.tt_title: The after-death Medicaid bill, explained. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
Medicaid estate recovery is federal law: states must seek repayment of long-term-care costs for enrollees 55 and older from the estate after death, at minimum from assets that pass through probate. States must waive recovery that would cause an undue hardship, and how far recovery reaches varies by state. Families who plan for care should ask about this rule before care starts, not after.

General info, not legal advice. Laws vary by state. Source: Medicaid.gov. AI-made visuals.
#wellkept #medicaid #estaterecovery #eldercare

beats: A 7 AM COLLECTION CALL?
Federal rule: before 8 AM and after 9 PM, your local time, is presumed an inconvenient time for collector calls.
They must also honor the times and places YOU tell them are inconvenient.
Know the window.
items.yt_title: Can a Debt Collector Call You at 7 AM?
items.tt_title: The 8-to-9 window on collector calls. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
Can a debt collector call you at 7 AM? Under the federal debt collection rule, calls before 8 AM or after 9 PM, your local time, are presumed to be at an inconvenient time, and a collector must also honor times and places you tell them are inconvenient. Exceptions exist, like your own consent.

Source: CFPB, Regulation F. Not legal advice. Laws vary by state. AI-made visuals.
#whattheycantdo #debtcollector #consumerrights #fdcpa

beats: SEVEN CALLS. SEVEN DAYS. THAT'S THE LINE.
Regulation F: more than 7 calls in 7 days about one debt, or a call within 7 days of speaking with you, is presumed to violate federal law.
The count runs per debt. Keep a call log.
Know the number.
items.yt_title: How Many Calls Can a Debt Collector Make in a Week?
items.tt_title: The 7-in-7 call rule. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
How many calls can a debt collector place in a week? Under Regulation F, calling more than seven times within seven days about a particular debt — or within seven days after a phone conversation with you — is presumed to violate federal law. The count runs per debt, and the presumption can be rebutted, so keep a dated call log.

Source: CFPB, Regulation F (12 CFR 1006.14). Not legal advice. Laws vary by state. AI-made visuals.
#whattheycantdo #debtcollector #consumerrights #regulationf

beats: BEFORE YOU PAY A DIME: PAPER.
A collector must send a validation notice: who they are, which creditor, the amount, and how to dispute.
It comes with the first contact or within five days after. Disputing in writing within 30 days pauses collection of the disputed amount until they verify.
Quiet holiday. Know your rights.
items.yt_title: What Must a Debt Collector Send You First?
items.tt_title: The validation notice, explained. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
Before you pay anything, a debt collector owes you paper: the validation notice naming the collector, the creditor, the current amount, and your dispute rights, delivered with the first communication or within five days after. Dispute in writing within 30 days and collection of the disputed amount pauses until they verify it. A calm right to know, for a calm holiday.

Source: CFPB. Not legal advice. Laws vary by state. AI-made visuals.
#whattheycantdo #validationnotice #debtcollector #consumerrights

beats: CAN THEY TELL YOUR BOSS?
No. A collector generally can't tell your employer, family or friends that you owe a debt.
They may contact others ONLY to find your address, phone or workplace, and if a lawyer represents you, they must call the lawyer.
Your debt is not office news.
items.yt_title: Can Debt Collectors Tell Your Boss About Your Debt?
items.tt_title: Your debt is not office news. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
Can a debt collector tell your boss about your debt? Generally no: under federal law a collector can't discuss your debt with your employer, family or friends. They may contact others only to locate you — address, phone, workplace — and if they know a lawyer represents you on the debt, they must go through the lawyer.

Source: CFPB. Not legal advice. Laws vary by state. AI-made visuals.
#whattheycantdo #debtcollector #privacy #consumerrights

beats: ONE LETTER. THE CALLS STOP.
Tell a collector in writing to stop contacting you, and they must stop — on every channel.
After that they may only confirm they're stopping or tell you about a specific step, like a lawsuit. The debt itself remains.
Send it certified. Keep a copy.
items.yt_title: The Letter That Stops Collection Calls
items.tt_title: THEY STOPPED: the written stop-contact right. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
You can tell a debt collector in writing to stop contacting you, and federal law says they must stop, on every channel. After your letter they may contact you only to confirm there'll be no further contact or to tell you about a specific remedy, like filing suit. The debt itself doesn't vanish, so weigh it first. The CFPB suggests certified mail and keeping a copy.

Source: CFPB. Not legal advice. Laws vary by state. AI-made visuals.
#whattheycantdo #stopcontact #debtcollector #consumerrights

beats: "PAY TODAY OR GO TO JAIL."
That threat is illegal. A collector can't threaten arrest over an unpaid consumer debt. It's harassment under the FDCPA.
The narrow exception is a court's own orders, like ignoring a summons. Court papers are never junk mail.
Report arrest threats to the CFPB.
items.yt_title: They Threatened Arrest Over a Debt. That's Illegal.
items.tt_title: Arrest threats over debt are illegal. Not legal advice.
items.caption:
"Pay today or go to jail" is an illegal threat: a debt collector can't threaten to have you arrested over an unpaid consumer debt — the CFPB treats that as FDCPA harassment. The narrow exception involves a court's own orders, like ignoring a summons, which is why court papers are never junk mail. Report arrest threats to the CFPB and your state attorney general.

Source: CFPB. Not legal advice. Laws vary by state. AI-made visuals.
#whattheycantdo #debtcollector #fdcpa #consumerrights
